package_info.package_name: Lumma Stealer (delivered via MediaFire spam campaign)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as executable via MediaFire, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware delivered as a standalone binary, not versioned via package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The distributed executable is identified as Lumma Stealer, a well-known infostealer malware. It is delivered through unsolicited spam comments on GitHub issues, luring users to download and execute a malicious file. The malware compromises the victim's system, steals sensitive data, and hijacks the user's GitHub account to propagate itself further.

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (after clicking spam link and executing downloaded file)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious executable downloaded from MediaFire (filename varies, e.g., .exe or .zip archive)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [Binary executable: Lumma Stealer payload, not shown as source code]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates browser-stored credentials, cookies, and environment variables, exfiltrates this data to a remote C2 server, and hijacks the victim's GitHub credentials to automate spam propagation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The executable is delivered via unsolicited spam comments and is identified as Lumma Stealer, a known infostealer. Its behavior includes credential theft, data exfiltration, and account hijacking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal executables downloaded from trusted sources should not access browser credentials, environment variables, or exfiltrate data. This malware violates user trust and system security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate system management tools may access some environment variables or browser data for backup or migration, but only with explicit user consent and never exfiltrate to unknown servers.
key_indicators: Unsolicited download link in GitHub issue comments
Executable accesses browser and system credentials
Automated use of victim's GitHub account for further spam

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (clicking spam link in GitHub issue comment)
execution_context.file_location: GitHub issue comment (spam message with MediaFire link)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Download this file from https://www.mediafire.com/file/xyz123/malware.zip and run it to fix your issue.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user reads the comment and clicks the link, they are directed to download a malicious archive from MediaFire, leading to execution of the malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited comments with download links to external file-sharing sites are a classic social engineering tactic. The link leads to a known malware payload.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal issue comments should not direct users to download and execute binaries from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate troubleshooting may involve sharing diagnostic tools, but these should be from trusted, verifiable sources and not via anonymous file-sharing services.
key_indicators: Multiple comments from new/unknown users in rapid succession
Links to MediaFire or similar file-sharing services
Instructions to download and run executables

attack_chain.action: Spambot posts unsolicited comments with MediaFire download links on GitHub issues.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is lured into downloading the malicious file.

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes the malicious file (Lumma Stealer) from MediaFire.
Malware steals credentials, exfiltrates data, and hijacks GitHub account to propagate spam.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further spread of spam and compromise of additional users.

behavioral_signatures: Unsolicited comments on GitHub issues containing links to external file-sharing services
Rapid posting of similar comments from multiple new or low-reputation accounts
Execution of binaries downloaded from MediaFire or similar platforms
Malware process accessing browser credential stores and environment variables
Automated posting to GitHub using compromised user credentials
file_indicators: Executable files or archives downloaded from MediaFire (e.g., malware.zip, random .exe files)
Unexpected binaries appearing in user download folders after clicking GitHub links
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Lumma Stealer C2 infrastructure
Unusual authentication attempts to GitHub from new locations/devices
HTTP/S POST requests containing credential data shortly after file execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unsolicited GitHub issue comments containing links to file-sharing services like MediaFire, especially from new or untrusted accounts. Flag and block downloads of executables from these links. On endpoints, detect execution of unknown binaries from user download folders, especially those that access browser credential stores or environment variables and initiate outbound connections to suspicious domains. Monitor for unusual GitHub account activity, such as automated posting or login attempts from new locations.
